Manufacturer should do a better job of identifying the electric thermal fuse from the gas one for the consumer. Paperwork that came with the set indicated different colors than were on the fuses to id the electric one from the gas. Fortunately the sticker on the packaging itself indicted the difference between the small fuses by listing the serial #, the serial # is then also found on the fuse body itself. The serial # entering with the letter T in my set is for gas dryers. The electric thermal fuse has a black body and the gas one a white body, in my set.

If you don’t happen to read the packaging or throw it away right away you may not be able to distinguish which fuse to use for electric dryers, apposed to gas dryers.

1) Ignore 'all' the instructions (the kit content, unit descriptions and color identification) that comes with the kit.
2) The kit comes with a cycling thermostat (larger unit) and 2 thermal fuses:
a) Electric dryer - Use the one rated to 150 Degrees Celsius. Approx. 302 Degrees Fahrenheit
b) Gas dryer - User the one rated to 115 Degrees Celsius. Approx. 239 Degrees Fahrenheit
3) FYI, once a fuse is blown (if the unit gets too hot) you have to replace it. Fuses only work once.
4) You should replace both the cycling thermostat and the thermal fuse since most of the time the reason for
which a thermal fuse is blown is because the cycling thermostat is faulty (... and you get both in the kit
anyways).
